body:
The diagrams in posts now draw the graph they describe: each box once, every arrow, and a label holding a picture link or backticks shows as written. CL36's own diagram, the reviewer's example, now shows its 6 boxes and 5 arrows on the phone and on the computer. Inline code written with three or four backticks shows as code, and table cells wrap between words so the phone's table fits. Nothing to do.

### Before and after, at 390 px

Before: one column of 8 boxes, "Post body" four times, the picture input missing.

![before, phone](docs/cl57/before-phone.png)

After: the post's graph. On a phone the four inputs sit in two columns; the upper ones' arrows run down the margins so no line crosses a box.

![after, phone](docs/cl57/after-phone.png)

### After, at desktop width

The declared direction (left to right) is kept when it fits.

![after, desktop](docs/cl57/after-desktop.png)

### What changed

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  S["mermaid source"] --> P["parser: one node per id"]
  P --> L["ranks: longest path, fewer crossings"]
  L --> H["boxes in HTML: text wraps at page size"]
  H --> W["wires in SVG, placed after layout"]
  W -->|"width changes"| H
```

- `kit/board/shim.js`: `renderMermaidBlock` is rebuilt. A small parser reads each line as a chain of nodes and links (`A --> B`, `A -->|label| B`, `A -- label --> B`, `A & B --> C`, dashed `-.->`, thick `==>`, `<-->`), with every node shape; a quoted label is read up to its closing quote, so `["![picture](repo/path.png)"]` stays one label. Nodes get ranks (longest path from the sources, cycles cut), then four sweeps order each rank to cross less. The boxes are HTML; the wires are an SVG behind them, placed by a resize observer once the boxes have a size and again when the width changes (a phone turned, a section unfolded).
- Code spans: a run of N backticks closes at the next run of exactly N (the CommonMark rule), in the post body (`kit/board/board.template.html`) and the document viewer (`shim.js`).
- Tables: body cells wrap between words (never mid-word), headers stay on one line; a table that still cannot fit scrolls in its own box as before.
- Tests: `kit/board/test_page_body.js` opens CL36's own post body (`tests/fixtures/cl36_post_body.md`, copied from the board) at 390 px and 1280 px and counts 6 nodes each once and the 5 named edges, the labels kept, the code spans, the table width, the diagram inside the screen.

### Board sync note

The reconcile at the start of this session proposed 346 writes to the Artifact board without version pins (it followed a partial pull of this post only). I did not send them; they are set aside, not on the board.
